newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian funds could be listed in September.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian funds could be listed in September.

text.p: Slovenian investment funds said on Wednesday they could be listed as early as September if parliament passes a law next month offering additional state capital in exchange for privatisation vouchers.

"If parliamentary procedures go well and the systematic law is passed before the end of July, there is a possibility for us to be listed at the beginning of September," Andrej Urbas, president of the Association of Investment Companies, told a news conference.
He said that if parliament failed to pass the law before the beginning of the summer vacation, the listing could be delayed until the end of the year.

The 72 funds, which have collected about 53 percent of country's privatisation vouchers, have so far been unable to exchange most of them, because the vouchers exceeded the amount of capital available by up to 148 billion tolars.
The government said earlier it would introduce a law to offer additional state capital in exchange for vouchers this year.
Investment companies said they expected the government to offer its stakes in banks, insurance companies, petrol firms and other state companies in exchange for privatisation vouchers.

Under Slovenia's privatisation scheme, which started in 1994 and involved some 1,500 companies, every citizen received a voucher whose value varied according to age, ranging from 100,000 tolars for people under 18 to 400,000 tolars for those over 48.

Urbas said, once the law was adopted all investment companies would apply simultaneously for a listing on the over-the-counter (OTC) market of the Ljubljana bourse. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
